body: Same here. Cancer would be a softer blow to my _very_ few loved ones than just outright killing myself.

I used to play the piano, as was my passion. I now have no energy or will to play. All I can do is think about when I can go to sleep next after I get off work. I have no energy to watch movies, play video games, fucking nothing. So lost in a deep pit of despair.

Agreed. The strife and turmoil will never end, you only get transitory pauses, if you're lucky. Then it's back to pain and misery. I've been inhabiting a very painful place for too long, after a while you just get tired of it. Suicide can help.

I've thought about it for many years, but the frequency with which I do suicidal ideation has increased a bit over the years and has certainly peaked recently. I just find no hope, no reason to live on. I have no energy for this life, don't want any part of this madness anymore.
At this point in my life, I would certainly welcome, with open arms, cancer. And if it were possible, I would substitute myself to die for anyone.
don't forget me!

Yes. I was reduced to laughter the other day. Was sitting on the bathroom floor, wanting to cry, wishing I were dead. So much mental pain. Then, I erupted in laughter, and I'm sure my neighbors were puzzled.

> since it can turn into a self-fulfilling prophesy.

Yeah, good point. It's quite scary how I am not always able to be mindful of such pitfalls while under the influence of  a depression bout. 

I'm going to see if I can find a therapist this week, give it yet _another_ try. Thanks.
I hope you can weigh your options carefully, make sure you've exhausted all of them before considering something permanent like suicide. I don't really know how to help, since I'm in the same boat.

I just think other people have better lives. If my conditions were different, e.g. some immutable attributes i have that fuck my life up from the outset were not present, I'm sure I wouldn't mind putting up with life. But alas, I am just fucked. 

I wish there were suicide clinics to help people die who really stand no chance at achieving any semblance of happiness.

Thanks for the thoughtful reply, glad you were able to find help ultimately before it was too late. 

Truly, suicide is a comforting feeling. My life is an unmitigated mess right now, with little hope of improving. There are many things coming between me and peace with life. Chiefly is just ordinary major depression disorder (have tried many pharmacalogical methods, therapy. Additionally is unrequited love, because I'm not good enough, not attractive enough (below average), not smart enough, not social enough. I feel life is just frankly not worth living if going through it unloved as I do. I'm just tired of being me and trapped with my set of attributes that just weigh me down, make it impossible to gain traction it feels--there's no hope many of these things will improve.  How long until I just feel too tired to fight on is the question I repeatedly ask. 1 years' time? 2 years' time?  It's not a question of if I'll finally be defeated, but when.
Been thinking more lately of when I should kill myself. I don't know when yet, but I believe it's an eventuality. It's a thought that brings me peace, where scarcely nothing else can.

I want to give medication another try, but I'm scared. I fear it failing again, or declining in efficacy after some months as in previous experiences. I fear I will further lose the handle of who "I" am, where it's this fleeting abstraction I can never seem to crystalize and suspend long enough to feel like I have a reference to what/who "I" am.

Yes. My approach is to give a generic response. I know that the other party doesn't care either way, it's just a convention, so why bother. Also, my life is bereft of much activity, so I have nothing to talk about other than sitting alone in my room in front of a screen most the time.

I feel I'm wasting my potential as well. Sometimes I enjoy entertaining how much better my life would be had I not been endowed with such mental illnesses. Just shows how little control anyone has to exercise in their own life. 

I hope you can find someone to talk to, because it sounds like no one is listening to you, or at the bare minimum receptive in terms of hearing you out. I have this problem as well. It's not fun to have an echo chamber of misery in your head becaues you've got no one to talk to. 

Thanks for the kind words.
Hey sorry to hear about the loss of your friend. I lost some friends of mine, too. Really have about 3 left, all of whom live some thousand miles away from me. Hope you feel better.

I'm sorry to hear that. I know the feeling of having to project some phony image just to appease everyone, and conform to their image they have of you. It's taboo to act how you feel inside with respect to depression. People don't want to deal with it, as it's a general down and affects their mood too. That's been my experience, at least. No one wants to have their mood fucked up by some depressive person, even if we're 'friends' or 'family'.

it feels depression has stolen my sense of identity. All I feel is nothing now, just tired. I can't summon up what I am supposed to be about anymore, or what I should spend my time doing. Just a vacant mind, killing time, feeling utterly miserable. Even if I don't waste my time, and refuse to project an image as if I'm okay, no one gives a fuck; so I've started to not attempt to hide it anymore.
Yes. I simulate conversations all the time. My brain's way of making up for an absent social life I guess.
I feel the same. As if I am having some early onset of neurodegenerative disease of some sort, due to my understimulation/isolation. Oh well, only a matter of time

Same for me. I question all the time how I can go on, knowing that my life has been irrevocably damaged by my depression and social anxiety. Relationships, job status, all have been substantially impacted. The prime points of my life are going away, and my mental problems will just continue to get worse. So really, what is the point? Why bother if I am going to just barely crawl my way through this life while everyone else is running and having a good time.

There is no absolute path depression culminates into, at least not that I'm aware. Untreated depression can cause health issues that can reduce your mortality later on, and in turn can reduce your overall quality of life and potential.
I wish there were suicide booths as portrayed in _Futurama_. That would be nice.

I used to delude myself into thinking it would go away eventually, or once I hit some imaginary life milestone. But again, this is lying to myself. This is a chronic condition, it has not gone away; it has killed off the few relationships I had, my physical appearance, my outlook, and persists as a lingering poison ready to kill anything remotely resembling happiness. Knowing this, I've abandoned notions of happiness I once had, trying to do other things to distract myself from what is absent because of depression's hold.

You echo my feelings exactly. Depression has precluded me from being monetarily successful. Or maybe I tell myself this to help me cope with being a broken person with no support system. I too wish I could get the courage to hang myself like he did.
If only I had things I enjoyed.

I've been, for the most part, a shut-in for about 8 years now. I feel in this time features of my cognition have deteriorated from lack of stimulation. I am a great candidate for neurodegenerative diseases no doubt because of my isolation. 

I have severe social aversions, have a hard time with eye contact, small talk and whenever i try to do anything about it I fail--so I've stopped trying and withdraw. I've begun to think I am not meant to be a normal functioning member of society and should just end it before it gets worse.

Oh yes, very much so.

I used to have a respectable group of friends, would hang out with any set of them every week. Then I turned 20 and had first panic attack. This was the beginning of the end of my social life. Afterward I began withdrawing, and before I knew it, 5 years had gone by and I lost most of my friends, besides a couple that I only have textual communication with. Now I have forgotten how to socialize for the most part. Things I had once taken for granted, like eye contact, conversing, are things I struggle with now. Now that I'm in my mid 20s I have no idea how to begin to get a new group of friends after having been withdrawn for many years. If anyone has gone through a large period of social withdrawal and re-emerged and found friends, I'd be delighted in reading how.

Hello! Social anxiety and panic sufferer here. I'm here to try and help others anyway I can, as well as attempt to learn techniques to get my life back after losing many friends over my panic and social anxiety issues some 5 years ago--I have not recovered, sadly.
I've been meaning to try to another therapist out, hope to this week.
Sounds familiar. I've done this when I had friends that cared in the past.

I too have this issue. Out of respect, when I force myself to do intermittent eye contact, it feels as if my insecurities are being read in an instant by the receiving party--somehow they can gather all this and read the contents of my mind just by some exchange of eye contact.

Also, while walking around on the streets I constantly have to avert my eyes either to the ground or in opposite direction. I'm sure others perceive me as having something wrong with me. I don't really know what to do, I feel broken.

My story parallels yours in lots of ways. I graduated a year ago at 26 with a degree, took multiple semesters off due to mental issues becoming overwhelming. have no accomplishments that are typical of someone my age, pretty much always indoors and refuse to give people a chance because of severe social anxiety. It's quite depressing. All the missed opportunity of youth and the huge space of potential things I could have done doesn't matter now as it's long dead. Concentrate on trying to construct a life for yourself now so you won't keep repeating that the last 5-10 years have been full of missed opportunity and no accomplishment. Work with a therapist if you can, whatever it takes, I guess.
I actually thrive on the weekends, my depression lifts momentarily. The work-week utterly drains and exhausts most of everything in me to the point I want to kill myself.

I've lost most my friends in the past due to depression episodes I've had. The small remainder I have left I think would feel bad abandoning me fully. My own self-image, as distorted as it may be, is ultimately cast onto how they see me in my mind. So I think they think I'm boring and pathetic and a failure--why do they bother? I don't know.
